question: Is the data actually exhausted, or was the count wrong because of operator error?
why_asked: The operator had made several errors this round (a state-schema misreading, an over-restriction on CC BY-NC, a misread of eligible_noncommercial_research_count). The owner was right to require an audit rather than an assurance.

verdict.licensed_tier: AT CEILING for samples. 204 coffees, 181 groups, 53 descriptors; upper bound if every unmapped atom were mapped is 214 coffees and 211 groups.
verdict.unlicensed_tier: NOT EXHAUSTED. 1,450 coffees and 1,420 groups, 7.8x the licensed tier, plus a ranked 200-item owner review packet already built and untouched.
verdict.operator_count_was_correct: 181 is confirmed three independent ways; it was not an undercount.
verdict.operator_report_was_incomplete: Earlier turns reported only the licensed tier and did not surface that the unlicensed tier is 7.8x larger and that its review queue is already prepared.

cross_validation_of_181.source: CROSS_FAMILY_SHARED_TARGET_BENCHMARK joined to the atom ledger, NC rows only

cross_validation_of_181.note: coffee count matches exactly; group count differs because R10 ran against the pre-round-2 registry

misclassification_found.found_in: the project's own rights matrix, not this round's work
misclassification_found.what: rights_product_deployment = PROHIBITED for 5,028 atoms, all of them family.zenodo_golovinsky_q_grader_dataset, the CC BY-NC source.
misclassification_found.why_it_matters: zenodo is the largest licensed source and supplies most of the 181 groups. The same atoms are AFFIRMATIVE_WITH_CONDITIONS for NONCOMMERCIAL_MODEL_RESEARCH. So under the matrix as written, the 181 groups may be used to research and evaluate, but not to deploy the product.
misclassification_found.assessment: The classification treats PRODUCT_DEPLOYMENT as inherently commercial. CC BY-NC restricts commercial use, not deployment as such, and a free personal PWA is not commercial use. The classification is over-strict for this project, but correcting it is an owner determination and a different question from R10's research GO.

vocabulary_situation.framing_correction: An earlier figure of 802 unmapped forms mixed the two tiers and overstated what the licensed tier offers.

unmapped_within_licensed_tier.meaning: vocabulary expansion available under the licence is about 40 concepts, not 800

vocabulary_situation.why_plain_text_is_not_readable: Every public-safe table stores hashed form ids; the surface column holds a category label, not text. Plain text sits behind restricted_pointer, a separate governance layer.

prepared_work_already_waiting.CRITICAL: 0 of the 200 are in the licensed tier. The entire prepared queue is unlicensed-tier material, so it unlocks nothing until the relabelling decision is made.

what_this_means_for_the_decision.option_A_stands: A was selected on 181 vs 0. The audit does not disturb that: the licensed corpus is specific-word data, which is what A needs.
what_this_means_for_the_decision.the_181_is_real_and_final: For evaluation of the non-fitting architecture, 181 groups covering 53 of 56 descriptors is the licensed ceiling and is adequate.
what_this_means_for_the_decision.the_growth_path_is_not_acquisition: More literature capture will not move these numbers; R10-R12 already demonstrated that, producing 6 groups from 248 candidates. The two levers are the ACE relabelling decision and user validation of the question axes.
